mission.cluster: the exclusive restart lock: declared transition edges, holder rules, bounded transition history and forced release

portedFiles.src/plugin/restart-lock.ts: restart-lock.mjs (with contracts.mjs carrying TRANSITIONS, REQUEST_STATE and the TransitionRefusal shape; the RestartLockState and RestartRequestState vocabularies come from the sibling restart-protocol module)

adaptation: TypeScript -> plain ESM JavaScript, Node 24, no new dependencies. The donor class becomes a factory-built object; the state machine, the holder rules, the bounded history and the forced release are carried over edge for edge.

The donor's single shared contract layer is preserved as a single source. `restart-lock.ts` imports `RestartLockState` and `RestartRequestState` from `../shared/protocol.js`; that shared layer is the sibling `restart-protocol` module in this same building, and `contracts.mjs` imports both vocabularies from `../restart-protocol/contracts.mjs` and re-exports them unchanged. The dependency direction is the donor's own (`plugin/* -> shared/*`), expressed as a cross-module import within the building, so there is exactly one declaration of each vocabulary and the lock cannot drift from the protocol it is part of.
`TRANSITIONS`, `REQUEST_STATE` and `TransitionRefusal` stay local, because the donor declares them in `restart-lock.ts` itself and nowhere else.

The donor declared `TRANSITIONS` at module scope and typed it as `Readonly<Record<RestartLockState, readonly RestartLockState[]>>`; that type constraint is what now enforces itself at runtime: every state name and every request state name passes through a validating copy-on-construct factory, and every table is a frozen lookup.

The donor's `TransitionRefusal` interface is exported as `transitionRefusal()`, a frozen copy-on-construct shape. `illegalTransition()` reproduces the donor's exact detail string, including `none` when a state has no declared successor, and `holderRequiredRefusal()` reproduces the exact holder refusal.

`release(reason)` validates its reason before it touches the lock, so a refused release leaves the state machine exactly where it was; the donor stamped the forced entry before it could be interrupted.

Every clock read goes through the injected `now`. The donor defaulted to `Date.now()`; this port never calls it and defaults to a fixed clock pinned at epoch 0 (`createFixedClock()`), so a lock built without an explicit `now` is deterministic until one is supplied.
`release` takes `reason`; the donor took `reason: string` and only returned it. The port builds the returned record through the contract factory, so the shape is validated and frozen.
Internal `record()` helper: appends one validated entry, then drops the oldest until `maxHistory` holds, restating the donor's `push` + `shift` bound in one place.
The donor's `RestartLock` class is exported as both `restartLock()` (factory) and `RestartLock` (alias), so the migration name survives without a class.
knownDifferences: No `Date.now` anywhere: `now` is injected and defaults to a fixed clock at epoch 0. The donor's `constructor(options: { now?: () => number } = {})` default was `() => Date.now()`; that default was deliberately not carried over, so `heldForMs()` is exact and tests are deterministic.

The donor's `get transitions()` returned a shallow copy of the history; this port copies the array and every record is a frozen shape, so a recorded transition cannot be rewritten after the fact. A caller that only reads the copy sees exactly the donor's array.

The donor performed no argument validation (TypeScript erased it). This port validates at the boundary: an unknown state name is a `TypeError` from the vocabulary gate, a non-integer `maxHistory` is a `TypeError`, and a non-function `now` is a `TypeError`. A known state that is simply not an allowed edge is still a returned refusal, never a throw, exactly as the donor returned it.

The donor `transition(to, holder)` had no JavaScript guard for a missing target; its `allowed.includes(to)` refusal could not have been built anyway, because a `TransitionRefusal` with no `to` is not the declared shape. This port refuses the missing target at the vocabulary gate with a `TypeError` and leaves the state untouched.

TypeScript interfaces (`TransitionRefusal`) and the compiled `readonly`/`private` modifiers have no JavaScript equivalent; they are replaced by frozen objects and closure state. No behaviour that depends on them was ported because the donor had none.

This module no longer declares the two vocabularies locally: they are imported from the sibling `restart-protocol` module, which is the port of `src/shared/protocol.ts`. The rest of that protocol (requests, tickets, supervisor, storage) remains out of scope here, as are `restart-executor`, `restart-supervisor` and every other donor module that consumed this lock.

Nothing in this module schedules, executes or observes a restart: it owns the invariant and the declared state machine, and it reports refusals instead of repairing them. The donor's crash reconciliation, ticket writing, shutdown port and audit log are not here.
`snapshot()`, `maxHistory` and the `createFixedClock()` helper are additions for porting and for the incubator surface; they read state the donor already tracked and change no rule.

vectors: the vocabulary is exactly IDLE, REQUESTED, CHECKPOINTING, SHUTTING_DOWN, RELAUNCHING, VERIFYING, and the request vocabulary is exactly rejected, queued, checkpointing, shutting_down, relaunching, verifying, completed, failed, cancelled

the declared edges are exactly IDLE:[REQUESTED], REQUESTED:[CHECKPOINTING, SHUTTING_DOWN, IDLE], CHECKPOINTING:[SHUTTING_DOWN, IDLE], SHUTTING_DOWN:[RELAUNCHING, IDLE], RELAUNCHING:[VERIFYING, IDLE], VERIFYING:[IDLE], and every declared edge is accepted
no undeclared edge is accepted: all 36 (from, to) pairs are walked and exactly the eleven declared edges move the lock
the refusal detail is exactly `illegal restart lock transition <from> -> <to>; allowed: <comma list or 'none'>` for a sample of illegal edges from every state
entering REQUESTED requires a non-empty holder, and the refusal is exactly `entering REQUESTED requires a request id`
the holder is set only on IDLE -> REQUESTED and cleared on -> IDLE, so a holder supplied to any other edge is ignored
heldForMs() is Math.max(0, now - enteredAtMs), is 0 on entry and never negative when the clock stands still or goes backwards
requestState maps IDLE:completed, REQUESTED:queued, CHECKPOINTING:checkpointing, SHUTTING_DOWN:shutting_down, RELAUNCHING:relaunching, VERIFYING:verifying
an accepted edge appends {from, to, atMs} with the injected clock reading
an illegal transition returns the refusal, changes no state, clears no holder and records no history entry
history is bounded by maxHistory (default 50) and drops the oldest record first; maxHistory 0 keeps nothing and maxHistory 1 keeps the newest
release(reason) returns null when already IDLE and otherwise forces IDLE, clears the holder and returns {from, reason} from every non-idle state
transitions returns a copy, so mutating the returned array does not touch the lock
every clock read goes through the injected now and the module contains no Date.now
the two vocabularies this module uses are the sibling shared layer's own frozen exports, so the vocabulary can be read from one source in the building and cannot drift

PARITY: the declared transition edges and both vocabularies
the refusal detail strings and the holder refusal
holder set/clear rules, heldForMs and requestState
release from every non-idle state and the already-idle null
PORT_ADAPTATION: TypeScript class -> factory-built object with closure state
interfaces -> frozen copy-on-construct factories that validate at the boundary
the shared contract layer kept as one source: the vocabularies are imported from the sibling restart-protocol module, the donor's plugin -> shared direction
injected clock with a fixed-epoch default instead of Date.now
frozen, validated transition records and snapshot
UTOPIA_EXTENSION: snapshot() frozen observable picture of state, holder, enteredAtMs and history
maxHistory exposed as a read-only bound
DEFERRED: the rest of the dsh-restart protocol (requests, status, cooldowns, crash loop)
